title: Regional Recovery Runner: orchestrated DR drills and health-validated cutover automation for Private VPC
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Goal: Build an automated 'Regional Recovery Runner' (RRR) that executes safe, repeatable, and observable DR drills for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments using Terraform modules and a small orchestration service. The RRR should: 1) provision a read-only standby region stack, 2) run preflight validators (data plane KV consistency, shard health, LB/ingress checks, KMS key availability), 3) exercise controlled promotion (DNS/route swap or ingress rebind) to the standby region under canary constraints, 4) run post-promotion smoke tests and health gates, and 5) perform automatic rollback and cleanup if any gate fails. Scope: Terraform module composition for reusable recovery artifacts (standby SGs, private endpoints, routing policies), orchestration controller (statemachine + SSM/SSH hooks), and a suite of health validators that integrate with Console tracing and runtime metrics. Out of scope: long-term cold-standby replication pipelines (separate project). Proposed approach: - Author a terraform/rrr module that composes existing VPC and runtime modules with an opinionated standby topology and tagging for drill metadata. - Add idempotent upgrade hooks that can apply minor runtime config changes in the standby region ahead of promotion (quantization profiles, kernel flags) via a 'dry-apply' plan step. - Implement a validator library: connectivity, kv-prefix-consistency, model artifact checksum, GPU readiness, and tail latency probes against a shadowed traffic generator. - Orchestrator will run as a short-lived runner in the control VPC (container job): create terraform plan, apply standby, perform validators, run canary promotion (meet SLOs: 95th latency <= X ms, error rate < Y), execute smoke-tests (end-to-end chat/generation and embeddings sample), and then either promote or revert. Safety & observability: - All steps logged to Console + dedicated run dashboard; change events annotated with run id and git SHA. - Rollbacks are automatic on validator fail; manual override requires two approvers (PM + SRE). - Rate-limit promotion via traffic shaping (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with telemetry gates per step. Acceptance criteria are listed separately. Implementation plan: 1) Terraform module skeleton + examples (2d), 2) Validator library and unit tests (3d), 3) Orchestrator prototype + local dry-run (3d), 4) Internal dry-run on demo tenant (2d), 5) First scheduled drill with canary (observability + incident retro) (2d). Deliverables: terraform module in infra/terraform/modules/rrr, orchestration service repo under infra/rrr-runner, runbook + Confluence doc, and one public postmortem style drill report. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: secret/KMS unavailability in standby — mitigate by pre-checks and key replication test. - Risk: terraform drift causing non-idempotent applies — mitigate with strict plan checks and stored plan artifacts. - Risk: customer data exposure during drills — mitigate by read-only standby by default and data masking where required.
acceptance_criteria: RRR terraform module can create a standby topology in a second region given a sample private tenant config
Preflight validators detect at least 4 possible failure modes (KMS, LB, KV, artifacts) and fail the run with actionable logs
Canary promotion can be executed at 10% traffic and safely ramp to 100% when telemetry gates pass
Automated rollback triggers on validator failure and returns primary traffic within the SLO window
A documented runbook and one successful internal drill report with metrics and lessons learned are published
